links.reason: The passage supports a distinct, orchestrated production pipeline with separate data-fetching and model-training components, but it does not specifically describe feature selection, transformation, combination, or preparation before algorithm use.

links.label: Time- and event-triggered training
links.description: Schedulers, calendar events, messages, monitoring events, or data and code changes initiate training.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes automated training triggered by a schedule or other triggers, with monitoring events also triggering pipeline execution.

links.label: Managed cloud MLOps platform
links.description: Adopt a fully managed cloud platform spanning substantial portions of model development and operations.
links.reason: The passage discusses assembling MLOps from cloud-compatible tools such as SageMaker, but advocates a custom multi-service ecosystem rather than adopting a fully managed cloud MLOps platform.

links.label: User-defined dataset validation
links.description: Custom routines detect inconsistencies, incorrect associations, missing values, and other data errors.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes user-defined validation routines that detect inconsistencies, incorrect associations, missing values, and other dataset errors.

links.label: Dedicated feature engineering pipeline
links.description: A distinct pipeline selects, transforms, combines, and prepares raw data before algorithm use.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes a distinct data engineering pipeline that cleans and transforms data to prepare training and testing datasets before use by ML algorithms.

links.label: Three-way prediction input contract
links.description: Supply predictions with model artifacts, processed data, and fresh live signals.
links.reason: The passage explicitly defines algorithms as handling three input types—models, previously processed data, and fresh live signals—matching the stated prediction input contract.

links.label: Schema-anomaly pipeline halt
links.description: Stop training or processing when incoming features are unexpected, missing, or invalid.
links.reason: The passage supports automatic schema/domain validation but does not state that processing or training halts when anomalies, missing features, or invalid inputs are detected.

links.label: Automated retraining-and-deployment pipeline
links.description: Pipeline automation that retrains, validates, and deploys models from offline development.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes an ML pipeline that automates retraining and deployment of new models, with CI/CD automating testing and deployment.

links.label: Neural architecture search
links.description: Automated search selects neural architectures using defined spaces, metrics, and search algorithms.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes NAS as searching defined architecture spaces, evaluating candidates with metrics, and using search algorithms such as random, gradient-based, and evolutionary methods.

links.label: Batch and real-time processing support
links.description: Accommodate both batch and real-time execution modes in the ML processing architecture.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that a production-ready ML system should support both batch and real-time processing.

links.label: Offline batch training
links.description: Training runs as an offline process rather than during prediction requests.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes offline computation as batch processing performed separately from real-time prediction, including periodic aggregation and precomputed results.

links.label: Notebook-based prototyping
links.description: Data scientists prototype with notebooks despite an enterprise-provided platform.
links.reason: The passage discusses prototyping and experimentation in Jupyter notebooks, but does not mention an enterprise-provided platform or adopting notebooks despite one.

links.label: Centralized consistent storage
links.description: Accessible data is retained in a consistent structure, ideally in one centralized location.
links.reason: The passage explicitly says data should be stored in a consistent structure and, ideally, conveniently in one place.

links.label: Multi-language implementation support
links.description: Use infrastructure that permits services or ML components to be implemented in multiple programming languages.
links.reason: The passage explicitly contrasts forcing data scientists to port code to R with allowing them to use code in their preferred framework, supporting multi-language implementation.

links.label: Containerized prediction microservice
links.description: A prediction model is packaged and deployed as a containerized microservice.
links.reason: The passage mentions support for containers and microservices, but does not clearly state that a prediction model is packaged and deployed as a containerized prediction microservice.

links.label: Automated ML lifecycle management
links.description: Automate training, deployment, retraining, and related lifecycle operations to reduce manual effort.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes automating the ML lifecycle, including training, deployment, retraining, continuous delivery, monitoring, and validation, to reduce manual effort.

links.label: Microservice architecture
links.description: Clearly separated product components are independently served as microservices.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes a serverless/microservice architecture with separate services and functions independently handling streams, monitoring, and model operations.

links.label: Single-objective error minimization
links.description: Considering one error objective instead of broader operational criteria was rejected for model assessment.
links.reason: The passage rejects relying solely on error minimization by emphasizing ongoing oversight of stability, ethics, fairness, explainability, user experience, and edge-case performance.

links.label: Local-machine data access
links.description: Develop by accessing protected data directly from a local machine.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that local-machine data access was not allowed and was rejected in favor of secure VM-based access.

links.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
links.description: Rely exclusively on software metrics to monitor a production model.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects relying only on software metrics, stating that this approach is insufficient for monitoring a production model.

links.label: Direct underlying-data access
links.description: Allowing direct access to underlying data was explicitly rejected as an infrastructure access approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that organizations do not want too many users to have direct access to the underlying data, indicating that this approach is rejected.

links.label: Business-KPI-only monitoring
links.description: Wait exclusively for downstream product or business KPIs to monitor model behavior.
links.reason: The passage explicitly rejects waiting exclusively for downstream business KPIs, stating they are too late and that dedicated ML monitoring is needed.

links.label: Active model performance monitoring
links.description: The source explicitly rejected active model-performance monitoring as the selected monitoring approach.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that level 0 lacks active performance monitoring, describing it as not tracking model predictions or actions to detect degradation.

links.label: Avoided repeated notebook computation
links.description: Avoid repeated expensive training, retrieval, or database computation through cached results.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes Jupyter caching cell results to avoid repeating expensive ML training, data retrieval, and database queries.

links.label: Improved transformation code quality
links.description: A structured development environment improves the quality of transformation code.
links.reason: The passage discusses data quality and fragile pipeline code but does not describe a structured development environment improving transformation code quality.

links.label: Managed platform flexibility and scalability
links.description: Flexibility and scalability resulting from using a fully managed platform.
links.reason: The passage identifies SageMaker as a fully managed end-to-end ML platform, but it does not explicitly describe the resulting flexibility or scalability.

links.label: Production accuracy requirement
links.description: Require AutoML-produced models to meet the accuracy needed for real-world use.
links.reason: The passage explicitly evaluates training options by accuracy and validates the selected model before deployment, indicating an accuracy/performance requirement for real-world use.

links.label: Partial monitoring coverage
links.description: Only a minority of deployed models receive monitoring, leaving substantial operational blind spots.
links.reason: The passage states there is no active performance monitoring, but it does not indicate that only a minority of deployed models are monitored or quantify partial coverage.

links.label: Model degradation
links.description: Changing real-world data causes predictive performance to decline over time.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that changing live data causes model predictive performance to decrease over time, defining model degradation.

links.label: Duplicated notebook queries
links.description: Repeated notebook query cells create duplicated query code.
links.reason: The passage explicitly states that using notebook cell magic can require duplicating identical queries and creating duplicate cells.

links.label: Data-type mismatch detection
links.description: Observed validation output identifying inputs whose types violate dataset expectations.
links.reason: The passage explicitly reports a Model Monitor datatype_check violation, identifying inputs with data types that violate expected types.

links.label: Replicable IDE code development
links.description: Use an IDE setup that supports proper, repeatable code and results.
links.reason: The passage explicitly requires identical development and production dependencies and technical stacks, plus containers or virtual machines to reproduce results.

links.label: Notebook showcasing and exploratory workflow
links.description: Use interactive notebooks for presenting results and conducting exploratory data analysis.
links.reason: The passage explicitly describes notebooks as interactive, sharable documents combining code, text, plots, and data-analysis tools, supporting exploratory and results-presenting workflows.
